class.name: FmodAudioEffectStereoEnhance
class.brief_description: Stereo enhancement effect for widening or narrowing the stereo field.
class.description: FmodAudioEffectStereoEnhance is a stereo widening/enhancement effect that can expand or contract the perceived stereo width of audio signals. It uses multiple techniques including pan pullout, time-based separation, and surround processing to manipulate the stereo image. The effect can create wider, more immersive stereo fields for music and sound effects, or narrow the stereo image for mono compatibility. Use it to add spaciousness to narrow recordings, create special stereo effects, or ensure mono compatibility when needed. Pan pullout scales the side signal around the average of the left and right channels across the full frequency range. With surround disabled, time pullout delays the right channel. With surround enabled, it delays the mid signal and adds it to the left channel while subtracting it from the right channel.

members.member: The side-signal multiplier used for stereo width, clamped to 0.0 through 4.0. At 0.0, the first two channels collapse to their mono average before delay or surround processing. The default 1.0 preserves their width; values above 1.0 widen the stereo difference.

The time-based stereo separation in milliseconds. Range: 0.0 to 50.0 ms. Default: 0.0. This introduces a small delay between the left and right channels to create stereo width. The effect mimics natural acoustic delays and can make sources sound wider. Higher values create more width but may cause comb filtering artifacts if too extreme. Use subtle values (1-10 ms) for natural enhancement.

The delayed mid-signal gain used for surround processing, clamped to 0.0 through 1.0. The default 0.0 disables surround processing. Positive values add the delayed mid signal to the left channel and subtract it from the right channel.
